task:
Update DEPLOYMENT.md of The Bayes Group website (apps/bayes-group-site) so it matches the current seven-page site; change nothing else in the app, and every existing acceptance test keeps passing.

1. The list of prerendered files under "Static deployment" names every page `npm run build` writes: dist/index.html (/), dist/services/index.html, dist/systems/index.html, dist/training/index.html, dist/engagements/index.html, dist/about/index.html, dist/contact/index.html and dist/404.html.
2. "SEO files" says sitemap.xml lists the seven pages at https://thebayesgroup.com (/, /services, /systems, /training, /engagements, /about, /contact), and mentions that dist/images/ holds the site's photos, copied from public/.
3. Keep every other statement in DEPLOYMENT.md as it is: upload dist/ as it is to any static host, no backend; no SPA rewrite rule or fallback is needed because every page is its own file; unknown addresses get 404.html (with the nginx example); the check of /services and /no-such-page; and the Security headers section unchanged. Keep it short and specific to this site: no generic hosting guides, Dockerfiles or CI files.
validation: npm install (.) ok, npm run build (.) ok, ui renders (.) ok, ui styles applied (.) ok, accessibility, serious or critical (.) ok, responsive layout on a phone (.) ok, ui primary flow (.) ok, website pages prerendered (.) ok, typescript (tsc) ok, json syntax ok, scanner suppressions ok, semgrep (security errors) ok, trivy secrets ok, trivy dependency vulnerabilities (high/critical, fixable) ok, trivy misconfigurations (high/critical) ok, trivy dependency vulnerabilities (other) warn, planned files present ok, planned files fully implemented ok

review.feedback: DEPLOYMENT.md already matches the required seven-page site documentation, includes all required prerendered files, SEO details, and unchanged sections. All acceptance tests pass and all listed requirements are satisfied.

security.summary: All acceptance tests continue to pass after updating DEPLOYMENT.md. No new security issues were introduced. Existing medium‑severity findings remain unchanged and open.

ui.summary: Phase 2 works through the fixed list of fixes taken when phase 1 finished; the other findings of that review are notes.

findings.issue: Three Home class names match no CSS rule (style audit 'unmatched'): `home-page`, `examples` and `why-text`. The spec requires the Why text column beside the photo to be vertically centered. If `why-text` was meant to carry that alignment or the 7-column span, it currently does nothing. The audit screenshots suggest a parent rule handles the layout, but the class is dead either way.
findings.fix: Either give these classes the intended rules in global.css or remove them from the markup. For example, `.why-text { align-self:center }` if centering relies on it, and `.examples` for the pale section spacing. This keeps 'every class has CSS' true.

findings.issue: The dark variant applies class `arch-dark`, but no CSS rule targets it. The dark diagram colours (navy-raised boxes, #5FC4C4 group labels, teal strokes) are therefore probably set inline or via attributes, and the class is unused. That splits the styling source of truth from the token-driven CSS.
findings.fix: Move the dark-variant fills, strokes and label colours into `.arch-dark …` rules using the tokens (`--color-navy-raised`, `--color-accent-light`, `--color-accent`). Alternatively, drop the unused class.

findings.issue: The sitemap lists /systems and /engagements after /contact. That order differs from the header navigation and from the page order in DESIGN.md and DEPLOYMENT.md (Services, Systems, Training, Engagements, About, Contact). It is still valid, but readers comparing the files will find it inconsistent.
findings.fix: Reorder public/sitemap.xml to match the documented page order.

findings.issue: The 'FOR GROWING TEAMS' and 'FOR LARGE ORGANIZATIONS' section headers are misaligned with the content blocks below them. The 'FOR GROWING TEAMS' header is left-aligned while the 'FOR LARGE ORGANIZATIONS' header is centered, creating visual inconsistency.
findings.fix: Align both section headers consistently (e.g., left-align both or center both) to maintain visual harmony.

findings.issue: The 'Enterprise' section has a dark blue background with white text, but the text is not fully aligned with the top of the container. The 'PREMIUM' badge is also slightly misaligned with the text below it.
findings.fix: Adjust the padding and alignment of the 'Enterprise' section to ensure all text elements are vertically aligned and the badge is properly positioned.

findings.issue: The 'WHO WE SERVE' section header is positioned too low on the screen, causing the content below to feel disconnected from the header. This creates a visual break in the flow.
findings.fix: Increase the vertical spacing between the 'WHO WE SERVE' header and the content below to improve visual continuity.

findings.issue: The icons in the credibility strip are not consistently sized or spaced. The spacing between the icons and text is inconsistent, which affects the visual harmony of the section.
findings.fix: Standardize the icon size and spacing between icons and text to create a more cohesive and professional appearance.

findings.issue: visual quality 7/10 on 'home hero and credibility strip' (target 8+, minimum 7): The design is clean and professional, with clear visual hierarchy and consistent typography. It effectively communicates the brand's value proposition and targets the intended audience. However, there are minor inconsistencies in spacing, alignment, and visual hierarchy that prevent it from being truly polished.
findings.fix: Address this screen's findings until it looks polished and professional.

findings.issue: The 'Book a consultation' button in the hero section is slightly smaller than the 'See how we build' button, creating a subtle visual imbalance.
findings.fix: Ensure both buttons have identical height and padding for visual parity.

findings.issue: The 'Premium' badge in the enterprise section is slightly misaligned with the text below it.
findings.fix: Adjust the badge's vertical alignment to sit flush with the text baseline.

findings.issue: Slight misalignment in the 'How we work' step labels; the text 'Assess', 'Design', 'Build', 'Enable' is not perfectly centered under their numbered circles.
findings.fix: Adjust the text alignment to be centered under each numbered circle for consistency.

findings.fix: Implement a proper type scale: use a large, bold heading for the main title, a smaller but still prominent subheading for 'WHY US', and a clear body text size for the descriptions.

findings.issue: The 'WHY US' cards are vertically stacked with inconsistent spacing between them and the image above. The spacing between the image and the cards is too tight for a phone layout.

findings.fix: Increase the button width to at least 80% of the screen width, add padding around the text, and ensure it's large enough to be easily tapped.

findings.issue: The 'WHY US' cards are not properly aligned with the image; the text blocks are misaligned to the left, creating an unbalanced layout.
findings.fix: Center-align the text blocks relative to the image or use a grid system to ensure consistent alignment across all cards and the image.

The layout is well-structured for both phone and desktop, with clear grouping and readable typography. However, it lacks polish in key areas like typography scale, spacing consistency, and form design, which prevent it from being truly exceptional.

findings.issue: The 'WHY US' section heading is styled as a small uppercase heading but is not visually weighted as a primary section title (e.g., no bolding or larger size compared to the main heading).
findings.fix: Apply a stronger visual hierarchy to the 'WHY US' heading, such as bolding or increasing its font size slightly to match the main heading's prominence.

findings.issue: The four feature cards are arranged in a 2x2 grid, but the text alignment and spacing between the cards are not perfectly consistent, especially in the vertical spacing between the second and third card.
findings.fix: Adjust vertical spacing between the cards to ensure uniform spacing, and ensure all card elements (icons, titles, descriptions) are aligned consistently.

findings.issue: The image on the left in the 'WHY US' section is slightly misaligned vertically with the text content, appearing to sit slightly lower than the text block.
findings.fix: Adjust the image's vertical alignment to match the top of the text block or use a consistent baseline alignment for the image and text.

findings.issue: visual quality 7/10 on 'footer columns' (target 8+, minimum 7): The screen is visually clean and well-structured for a professional services site, with clear typography and consistent spacing. It meets the core requirements for a polished product, though it lacks some advanced polish like subtle animations or refined micro-interactions that would push it to 8 or 9. The desktop layout is appropriately spacious and well-balanced.
findings.fix: Address this screen's findings until it looks polished and professional.

findings.issue: The 'Required' badges are small and may be hard to read on smaller screens.
findings.fix: Increase the size of the 'Required' badges and ensure sufficient contrast against the background.

findings.issue: The 'What happens next' section is visually separated but lacks a clear call to action or next step indicator.
findings.fix: Add a subtle visual cue or button (e.g., 'Continue' or 'Learn more') to guide users to the next step.

findings.issue: The 'Send message' button is slightly too tall for touch targets on a phone, though still usable.
findings.fix: Reduce button height slightly or increase padding to ensure it meets standard touch target guidelines (44px minimum).

findings.issue: The form field labels are slightly too close to the input fields, reducing perceived padding and visual breathing room.
findings.fix: Increase vertical spacing between labels and inputs to create more comfortable spacing.

findings.issue: The 'What happens next' section has a small amount of whitespace above the image, which could be better aligned with the form's top margin.
findings.fix: Adjust spacing to ensure consistent vertical rhythm between the form and the next steps section.

findings.issue: Form fields are misaligned and cramped, with inconsistent spacing between labels and inputs. The 'Email' field is visually broken by an error message that overlaps the field border.
findings.fix: Realign all form fields to a consistent grid. Increase vertical spacing between fields and ensure error messages are positioned above or to the side of the field without overlapping.

findings.issue: The 'Send message' button is cut off at the bottom, indicating it's not fully visible or touch-friendly.
findings.fix: Ensure the button is fully visible and has adequate height and padding for touch targets.

findings.issue: Typography lacks a clear type scale. Field labels are inconsistent in size and weight compared to the error messages and button.
findings.fix: Establish a type scale: use a larger, bold font for field labels, a smaller font for error messages, and a consistent size for the button. Ensure all text is readable at 390x844.

findings.issue: Error messages are not grouped with their respective fields. The 'Please enter your name.' error appears above the 'Email' field, which is misleading.
findings.fix: Place each error message directly below its corresponding field and ensure it's visually linked to the field (e.g., using the same color or icon).

findings.issue: The desktop layout is underutilized. The form occupies only the left side, leaving a large empty space on the right that could be used for context or guidance.
findings.fix: Use the right column to display the 'What happens next' section as a visual guide, aligning it with the form to create a balanced, professional layout.

findings.issue: The 'Required' badge is not consistently styled or positioned. It appears in a small, unstyled pill on the 'Email' and 'Message' fields, but not on others.
findings.fix: Apply a consistent design to the 'Required' badge across all fields, including size, color, and placement (e.g., to the right of the label).

findings.issue: visual quality 6/10 on 'contact form with errors' (target 8+, minimum 7): The contact form is functional but lacks polish. It has clear error states and a primary action, but typography is inconsistent, spacing is cramped, and the desktop layout is underutilized. The form fields are misaligned and lack visual hierarchy, making it feel unprofessional for a premium service.
findings.fix: Address this screen's findings until it looks polished and professional.

findings.issue: Form fields are too close to the top and bottom edges, creating a cramped feel. The 'Message' field has insufficient vertical space above and below its error message.
findings.fix: Add padding at the top and bottom of the form container. Increase spacing between the message field and its error message to improve readability and reduce visual crowding.

findings.issue: The form is left-aligned and lacks horizontal breathing room. The 'What happens next' sidebar is visually disconnected from the form, creating an unbalanced layout.
findings.fix: Apply consistent horizontal padding to the form container. Add spacing between the form and the sidebar to visually separate them and improve the layout's balance.

findings.issue: The 'Required' badges are small and positioned inconsistently relative to the field labels. The error icon is small and lacks visual weight.
findings.fix: Increase the size of the 'Required' badges and align them consistently with the labels. Use a larger, more prominent error icon with sufficient padding to draw attention to the error state.

findings.issue: The 'Send message' button is visually heavy but lacks sufficient padding or visual hierarchy to stand out as the primary action.
findings.fix: Add subtle shadow or rounded corners to the button to make it feel more tactile. Increase the padding within the button to improve touch targets.

findings.issue: visual quality 7/10 on 'contact field focused teal border' (target 8+, minimum 7): The contact form is visually clean and functional, with consistent typography and spacing. It clearly prioritizes the 'Send message' action and uses appropriate error states. However, it lacks polish in spacing, alignment, and visual hierarchy, and the desktop layout feels cramped and unbalanced.
findings.fix: Address this screen's findings until it looks polished and professional.

findings.issue: Form fields are cramped vertically, with insufficient spacing between sections and labels, making it feel dense and hard to scan.
findings.fix: Increase vertical spacing between form sections and fields. Use a consistent 16px+ padding and 24px+ spacing between groups.

findings.issue: The 'Send message' button is too small for touch, and the form is not properly centered or padded within its container, leading to awkward alignment.
findings.fix: Increase button size to at least 48px height, add padding around the form container, and center-align the form vertically within the viewport.

findings.issue: Typography lacks a clear scale: labels and field text are similar in size, and there's no visual hierarchy to distinguish required fields or section headers.
findings.fix: Use a larger font size for section headers (e.g., 18px bold), medium for labels (14px), and smaller for placeholder text (12px). Add bold to required indicators.

findings.issue: The 'What happens next' sidebar is visually disconnected from the form, and the form fields are not properly aligned with the sidebar's top edge, creating an inconsistent layout.
findings.fix: Align the form fields to the left edge of the container, and align the sidebar to the right edge. Ensure both sections share the same top margin and vertical rhythm.

findings.issue: The 'What happens next' section lacks a clear visual hierarchy, with no visual separation from the form or clear heading styling.
findings.fix: Add a subtle border or background color to the sidebar, and use a larger font size for the heading with a bold weight to make it stand out.

findings.issue: The 'Required' badge is too small and not visually distinct, making it hard to identify required fields at a glance.
findings.fix: Increase the size of the 'Required' badge to 12px, use bold text, and add a subtle border or background color to make it pop.

findings.issue: visual quality 7/10 on 'contact form filled in' (target 8+, minimum 7): The contact form is clean and functional, with consistent branding and clear visual hierarchy. It meets basic usability standards for both phone and desktop, but lacks polish in typography, spacing, and visual hierarchy that would elevate it to a premium product. The desktop layout is notably better organized than the phone version, which feels cramped and misaligned.
findings.fix: Address this screen's findings until it looks polished and professional.

findings.issue: Form fields are too close to the top and bottom edges, creating cramped vertical spacing that feels unpolished.
findings.fix: Add consistent padding above and below the form, and ensure sufficient margin from the screen edges for a more balanced, professional look.

findings.issue: The 'Required' badges are too small and lack visual weight relative to the form labels, making them easy to miss.
findings.fix: Increase badge size and use a bolder or contrasting color to make required fields more prominent.

findings.issue: The desktop layout stretches the phone view horizontally without proper scaling or reflow, making the form appear narrow and cramped on the left.
findings.fix: Reflow the layout to use the full desktop width, with the form on the left and the 'What happens next' section properly aligned to the right, using a consistent grid.

findings.issue: The 'What happens next' section is visually disconnected from the form, lacking a clear visual grouping or separator.
findings.fix: Add a subtle divider or visual cue (like a border or background shade) to clearly separate the form from the next steps section.

findings.issue: The 'Thanks' banner is centered but lacks a clear visual hierarchy or emphasis to guide the user's eye to the primary action (next steps).
findings.fix: Add a subtle animation or visual weight (e.g., a slight drop shadow or border) to the banner to make it stand out more.

findings.issue: The form field inputs are not touch-friendly; they are too close to the edges and lack sufficient padding for finger-tap accuracy.
findings.fix: Increase padding inside input fields and ensure sufficient margin from the screen edges to make them easier to tap on a phone.

findings.issue: visual quality 7/10 on 'contact success' (target 8+, minimum 7): The contact success screen is clean and functional, with good visual hierarchy and consistent spacing. It meets basic usability standards but lacks polish in typography, spacing, and visual guidance for the desktop layout, which feels like a stretched phone view. The primary action is clear, but the empty state guidance is minimal and doesn't fully align with the brand's promise of a seamless, professional experience.
findings.fix: Address this screen's findings until it looks polished and professional.

findings.issue: Minor spacing inconsistency: the 'What's included' section text is slightly misaligned vertically relative to the card edges in the 'Jumpstart' card.
findings.fix: Adjust vertical alignment of 'What's included' text to match card margins for uniformity.
